findings.description: The rule that converts scored or determined values into a conformity or grade decision, the cut scores, acceptance limits and guard bands it uses, how uncertainty is accounted for beforehand, and the conditions under which the assessment must abstain.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The decision rule must be machine-readable inline so a consumer can re-derive the conclusion from the recorded values. Where the rule is published by a scheme or laboratory quality system, it is referenced by identifier and version; enforcing or executing the rule against live systems belongs to the referenced enforcement model, not here.

bundles.name: Evidence and Observation
bundles.description: What was relied on, how it links to criteria, whether it is sound, and what was actually observed.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL separates observations carrying evidence from findings that judge criteria; SP 800-53A ties evidence to determination statements; EARL requires a subject and a test behind every result. Evidence handling is therefore a distinct top-level concern from determination, and its quality qualifiers decide whether a conclusion is defensible.

layers.name: Evidence Corpus
layers.description: The evidence items relied on, their linkage to criteria, and their quality and admissibility.

findings.name: Evidence items and criterion linkage
findings.description: The discrete evidence items relied on, their types, the criterion or determination statement each supports or contradicts, and the times at which each was created, collected and received.

findings.name: Evidence quality, admissibility and reuse limits
findings.description: Whether each item is authentic and unaltered since collection, whether it is still current for the assessed state, which offered evidence was rejected or down-weighted, and which items carry confidentiality or personal-data constraints limiting reuse.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Quality qualifiers are assertions attached to evidence already registered by the linkage finding: digests, expiry dates, exclusion reasons and sensitivity codes. The evidence bytes are held by the referenced custody model and the artifact for them is declared once, so restating them here would create a second registration of the same object.

layers.name: Observation and Measurement
layers.description: Raw observed results with distinct event and recording times, and the uncertainty and traceability that qualify quantitative values.

findings.name: Observation records, actors and timing
findings.description: The raw result observed or returned for each check before judgement is applied, the actor or device that produced it, the separation of the time the observed condition held from the time the observation was recorded, and the place of observation where it matters.

findings.name: Measurement uncertainty and traceability
findings.description: The stated uncertainty of each quantitative result and how it was evaluated, the quantity, unit and reference scale each value belongs to, and the calibration or reference standard the measurement is traceable to.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Uncertainty statements, units and traceability pointers are declared values carried alongside each quantitative result. Calibration certificates and the traceability chain are produced and maintained by the referenced metrology model; this model neither runs calibration programmes nor issues those certificates, so it declares no artifact for them.

bundles.name: Determination, Scoring and Conclusion
bundles.description: Criterion-level verdicts and scores, their aggregation into a composite result, and the stated conclusion with its validity.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC 17000 distinguishes determination from review and from decision; OSCAL distinguishes observations from findings; XCCDF distinguishes rule-results from a scored TestResult. This bundle keeps criterion-level determination, aggregation and the accountable conclusion as separate, traceable steps rather than collapsing them into a single verdict.

layers.name: Criterion-Level Outcomes
layers.description: Per-criterion verdicts with rationale and locators, and the raw and normalised scores that accompany them.

findings.name: Criterion verdict, rationale and locator
findings.description: The outcome value assigned to each criterion from the bound vocabulary, the reasoning connecting cited evidence to that outcome, the severity or materiality of negative outcomes, and where in the subject each negative outcome occurs.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Criterion outcomes are structured values keyed to criterion identifiers and must be queryable, sortable and diffable as data rather than read out of a rendered document. The report that presents them to a reader is declared once by the conclusion finding, which keeps a single authoritative rendition.

findings.name: Criterion scores and normalisation
findings.description: The raw score recorded for each criterion against its maximum, how raw scores are normalised or rescaled before aggregation, and which scale definition version each recorded score refers to.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Scores are numeric data bound to a scale reference and must be recomputable and comparable across records. QTI keeps outcome variables as declared data separate from results reporting, and this finding follows that separation; the rendered scorecard is declared by the aggregation finding.

layers.name: Composite Result, Conclusion and Validity
layers.description: How criterion results roll up, what conclusion is stated and by whom, and for how long and under what conditions it holds.

findings.name: Aggregation model and composite result
findings.description: The scoring or aggregation model that combines criterion results, the weights and precedence rules it applies, the form in which the composite is expressed, and how it is computed when some criteria are untested or indeterminate.

findings.name: Conclusion statement, authority and qualification
findings.description: The stated conclusion and its form, the actor accountable for it and whether the decision was separated from the determination work, the qualifications, adverse opinions or dissent attached, and what the conclusion entitles or obliges.

findings.name: Validity window, conditions and confidence
findings.description: From when until when the conclusion is asserted to hold, the conditions whose breach voids it early, the surveillance or re-assessment needed to keep it current, and the confidence or assurance level claimed.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity is expressed as timestamps, conditions and a claimed assurance level that consumers must evaluate programmatically before relying on a conclusion. Surveillance activities themselves are executed under the referenced scheme or programme model, and any certificate that carries these dates is issued by the attestation model.

bundles.name: Assurance of the Assessment Itself
bundles.description: Whether the people, tools and instrument behind the result can be relied on.
bundles.rationale: EU law makes legal effect depend on the designation of the body rather than the quality of the method; ILAC and ISO/IEC 17025 make impartiality and competence preconditions of a statement of conformity; and the AERA/APA/NCME Standards make validity, reliability and fairness foundational. Assurance of the assessor and the instrument is therefore a separate concern from the result itself.

layers.name: Assessor and Independence
layers.description: Who performed the assessment, in what roles, with what competence and authorisation, and under what declared conflicts.

findings.name: Assessor identity, roles and contribution
findings.description: Which persons, teams, bodies or automated agents performed the assessment, how the roles of collecting, determining, reviewing and deciding were distributed, and which parts of the result are attributable to which agent.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Assessor identity and role assignment are references into the party model plus PROV-style attribution links. Personnel records, employment status and organisational structure are maintained by that referenced model, so this finding holds pointers and role codes only.

findings.name: Competence, authorisation and impartiality
findings.description: The competence, qualification or accreditation supporting each assessor's participation, the designated scope within which the assessing body may act, declared relationships that could impair impartiality, and what the assessment explicitly does not entitle the assessor to assert.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Competence, accreditation and designation are asserted and maintained by accreditation authorities and party registries; this finding carries their identifiers, validity and scope plus a locally authored conflict declaration. Reproducing accreditation certificates here would copy content owned by the accreditation registry and risk asserting a status this model cannot verify.

layers.name: Quality Control and Instrument Quality
layers.description: Review and moderation of this assessment, and the standing evidence that the instrument measures what the conclusion claims, reliably and fairly.

findings.name: Review, moderation and rater agreement
findings.description: The independent review, second marking or moderation performed before finalisation, the inter-rater or inter-tool agreement measured against a threshold, and how disagreements between assessors or tools were resolved.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Review is a function of this assessment recorded as structured events, statistics and outcomes attached to the record. ISO/IEC 17000 treats review as an internal function preceding the decision rather than a deliverable, and the review's visible output is carried in the assessment report already declared.

findings.name: Instrument validity, reliability and fairness evidence
findings.description: The standing evidence that the instrument measures what the conclusion claims, that its results are precise and repeatable, that bias and accessibility barriers across subject groups have been checked, and the populations or contexts for which it is not validated.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, Disclosure and Interoperability
bundles.description: How the record moves through its states, how it is corrected and challenged, who may see what, how long it is kept, and how it projects into external formats.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL requires record identity and last-modified to change on every content change; FHIR supplies an explicit status vocabulary including entered-in-error; the AERA/APA/NCME Standards give test takers rights that imply an appeal route; EU law limits who may publish a result with legal effect; and EARL, XCCDF, OSCAL and QTI all define incompatible result vocabularies that must be crosswalked deliberately.

layers.name: Record Lifecycle
layers.description: States and transitions of the assessment record, and how it is corrected, challenged and superseded.

findings.name: Assessment state and transitions
findings.description: The states an assessment record may occupy and the vocabulary defining them, the permitted transitions with their actors and preconditions, what becomes immutable at finalisation, and how a record that should never have existed is marked without erasing its history.
findings.inline_only_rationale: States and transitions are control data on the record, consumed by callers to decide whether a conclusion may be relied on. The platform's change history and access log are owned by the referenced audit model, so this finding records status and transition times without producing or owning an audit artifact.

findings.name: Correction, appeal and supersession
findings.description: When an amendment is required rather than a new assessment, how the subject or a relying party may challenge the conclusion and within what period, how the outcome of a challenge is reflected, and how the chain from the original to the currently effective conclusion is navigated.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Correction and supersession are expressed as reason codes, pointers and flags that let a consumer resolve the currently effective conclusion. Appeal case files, hearings and their procedural conduct are handled by the referenced dispute or case-management model; this finding retains only the reference and the recorded outcome.

layers.name: Disclosure and Retention
layers.description: Who may see which part of the record, what is redacted before release, and how long each part is kept before disposition is referred onward.

findings.name: Disclosure classification and redaction
findings.description: The disclosure class applying separately to the conclusion, the scores and the underlying evidence, the terms under which the assessment may be published or cited, what must be redacted before external release and who approves it, and whether a conclusion may be released without its evidence.

findings.name: Retention class and disposition referral
findings.description: The retention class and trigger applying to each part of the record, which policy and system execute destruction or transfer when retention ends, and how a legal hold or open appeal suspends disposition.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Retention here is a declared classification, a trigger event and a pointer to the owning records-management policy, plus a record that the referral was made. Setting periods and executing destruction, transfer or erasure — and issuing any destruction certificate — belong to that referenced model, so producing an artifact here would assert ownership of disposition this model does not hold.

layers.name: Interoperability
layers.description: Projection into external assessment reporting formats and binding of the vocabularies, units and languages used.

findings.name: External alignment and vocabulary binding
findings.description: Which external assessment reporting formats this record must project into, how local outcome values map into each target vocabulary and where that mapping loses information, which code systems, units and language tags are bound at which versions, and what is claimed as conformance to an external standard.

model.name: Organizational Unit
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to understand, create, inspect and operate the internal structure of an organization: which units exist, how they nest and report, what each is mandated to do, what establishment and staffing they carry, and how that structure is changed, dated, evidenced and disclosed over time.
model.scope_statement: This model covers an organizational unit as a subdivision that, in the words of the W3C Organization Ontology, 'only has full recognition within the context of that Organization'. It governs unit identity, classification, containment and reporting relationships, delegated mandate and decision rights, authorized establishment and measured staffing, structural change acts and their temporal validity, plus the provenance, retention, disclosure and interoperability rules that make the structure record operable. It deliberately stops at the boundaries of legal organizational identity, of the post/position as an object in its own right, of employment relationships, of physical sites, and of statistical or financial reporting units that are derived from - but not identical to - internal structure.
in_scope: Unit identity, naming, aliases and parent-scoped or ISO/IEC 6523 organization-part identification
Unit kind classification against governed code lists and unit existence status
Containment hierarchies, including multiple concurrent hierarchies (managerial, legal, cost, functional)
Reporting and coordination lines, including non-containment and dotted-line relationships
Delegated mandate, decision rights, authority limits and segregation-of-duties constraints attached to a unit
Authorized establishment (post complement) seated in a unit and its occupancy state at unit granularity
Dated headcount and full-time-equivalent measurement of a unit, with basis and aggregation thresholds
Reorganization acts (create, rename, reparent, merge, split, transfer, disband) and unit lineage
Effective dating, bitemporality and as-of reconstruction of the structure graph
Record authority, approval evidence, retention/disposition and disclosure control for structure data
Crosswalks to W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR, LDAP, SCIM, schema.org and ISO/IEC 6523 projections
out_of_scope: Legal personality, incorporation, registration, LEI and regulatory identity of the whole organization (WM-ORG-001)
The post/position as an object with its own title, grade, job description and occupational classification (WM-ORG-004)
Employment contracts, appointments, persons and their occupancy of posts
Constitutive charter powers of the organization as a legal entity (charter model)
Physical premises, addresses, geometry and site operations (site/location model)
Statistical units such as enterprise, local unit and kind-of-activity unit used for economic observation
Financial segment reporting, general ledger and cost accounting mechanics
Stewardship policy machinery and access-grant issuance (S1/S2 service models)
Business capability, process and value-stream modelling
Identity-provider group membership and directory synchronisation state as a system of record

boundary_notes.distinction: W3C ORG separates org:FormalOrganization (recognized in a legal jurisdiction, with rights and responsibilities) from org:OrganizationalUnit, which has full recognition only inside its parent. Legal identity, registration and LEI stay in WM-ORG-001. A branch that is separately registered is dual-classified: it is a unit here and a legal entity there, and GLEIF only issues an LEI to the legally registered entity, not to an internal division.

org:Post represents a position that exists independently of who fills it. This model records only the unit-side facts: how many posts are established in the unit, which posts are seated there, and the aggregate occupancy state. Post title, grade, competency profile and occupational classification belong to WM-ORG-004, which this model CONTAINS by reference rather than by copy.

FHIR states that Location records where a service occurs while Organization records who performed it; Eurostat's 'local unit' is 'an enterprise or part thereof ... situated in a geographically identified place'. A unit may be associated with one or more sites, but premises, addresses and geometry are not unit attributes and are not modelled here.

Council Regulation (EEC) No 696/93 defines enterprise, kind-of-activity unit and local unit as observation units for economic statistics. These are derived by statistical rules from operational reality, not asserted by the organization, and their boundaries routinely differ from internal units. Treated as an ALIGN target, never as a source of internal unit identity.

IFRS 8 identifies operating segments through a management approach based on how the chief operating decision maker reviews internal reports, and permits aggregation of segments with similar economic characteristics. A reportable segment is therefore a derived view over internal units, not a unit; this model supplies the inputs and the change signal, not the segment determination.

RFC 4519 defines 'ou' as a multi-valued name attribute and RFC 7643 defines SCIM 'department', 'division' and 'organization' as free-text names. These carry no identifier, no validity period and no hierarchy semantics, so directory content is a lossy projection of this model and never its system of record.

ROR states it 'is not focused on capturing all subdivisions of a given organization such as a university's schools or departments' because departments 'often emerge, close, combine, and change'. No general governed global identifier exists for internal units, so unit identity is parent-scoped by default.

functions.name: Resolve Unit Identity
functions.description: Resolve any inbound reference - master-system identifier, ISO/IEC 6523 organization part identifier, alias, former name, LDAP distinguished name or IdP group id - to the single current unit record or to a tombstone with a successor pointer.
preconditions: The unit register is loaded for the stated parent organization
The alias and lineage indexes cover the requested as-of instant
effects: Emits a resolution audit entry with the input, method and outcome
Never mutates the unit record

functions.name: Validate Structure Graph
functions.description: Evaluate integrity rules over a structure version: acyclicity within each named hierarchy, single parent per hierarchy per validity interval, no orphans, referential integrity to WM-ORG-001 and WM-ORG-004, temporal gap and overlap rules, and segregation-of-duties constraints.
outputs: validation result set with severity per finding
preconditions: The structure version is fully materialised and immutable
The rule set version is published and resolvable
effects: Produces a Structure Validation Report artifact
May block a pending write when blocking failures are present

functions.name: Reconstruct Structure As Of
functions.description: Return the unit set, hierarchies, reporting lines and mandates valid at a given world-time instant as recorded at a given record-time instant, producing a deterministic, digest-identified view.
outputs: Structure As-Of View with structureVersionId and content digest
list of elements excluded by disclosure class
preconditions: Bitemporal stamps exist on all included assertions
The requested instants fall inside the reconstruction horizon
effects: Materialises a frozen, immutable as-of export
Records the query parameters and digest for reproducibility

functions.name: Apply Reorganization Act
functions.description: Apply an evidenced structural change - establish, rename, reclassify, reparent, merge, split, transfer or disband - creating lineage edges, closing and opening validity intervals, and registering downstream obligations.
inputs: reorganization act record with kind and affected units
outputs: updated unit records with closed and opened validity intervals
preconditions: The deciding body holds the delegated authority for the act kind
Pre-commit validation passes or an approved override exists
Any jurisdictional consultation precondition is evidenced as complete
effects: Mutates the structure graph as of the effective instant
Produces a Reorganization Decision Record artifact
Notifies segment reporting, directory provisioning and contract owners

functions.name: Derive Org Chart Projection
functions.description: Generate a hierarchy view for a named hierarchy at an as-of instant, containing unit names and kinds only, with mandate detail and staffing deliberately excluded.
preconditions: The named hierarchy exists and has valid edges at the as-of instant
The requesting principal holds read scope for the hierarchy
effects: Emits a serial projection instance bound to its source structure version
Marks the output as non-authoritative and non-reimportable

functions.name: Evaluate Mandate Conflict
functions.description: Detect overlapping or incompatible remits across units and breaches of authority limits or independence requirements, before or after a proposed structural change.
outputs: conflict findings with affected units and rule references
preconditions: Mandates are expressed with structured scope, not narrative only
The rule set encodes incompatible mandate pairs
effects: Records conflicts as validation findings with severity
Triggers a waiver workflow when an exception is sought

functions.name: Compute Headcount Rollup
functions.description: Aggregate staffing measurements up a named hierarchy under a declared counting basis and period convention, applying suppression where a cell falls below the minimum size.
outputs: rolled-up figures per unit with basis and period stated
suppression markers distinguishing suppressed values from true zeros
preconditions: Underlying snapshots share a compatible basis and population definition
The minimum cell size policy is resolved for the audience
effects: Appends to the Headcount Snapshot Series artifact
Logs each suppression with the rule applied

functions.name: Reconcile External Directory
functions.description: Compare LDAP or SCIM representations of units against the governed structure, report drift, and push corrections outward without ever accepting the directory as a source of truth.
inputs: directory export (LDAP entries or SCIM Groups and Enterprise User attributes)
outputs: drift report of name, membership and hierarchy differences
preconditions: A mapping from unit identifiers to directory distinguished names or group ids exists
The directory export carries a generation timestamp
effects: Never mutates the governed structure from directory content
Queues outbound provisioning changes and records unresolved name-only matches

functions.name: Emit Standards Mapping
functions.description: Serialise the structure into a target vocabulary - W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR Organization, schema.org, or an ISO/IEC 6523 party identifier - using the versioned crosswalk and attaching a fidelity declaration.
preconditions: A crosswalk entry exists for every included element and target version
No conformance claim is asserted without a referenced test result
effects: Produces a serial export bound to the crosswalk version used
Records any element dropped for lack of a target term

functions.name: Apply Disposition
functions.description: Execute the approved retention schedule over structure records: destroy, transfer to archive or flag for review, while preserving the tombstones and lineage edges required for historical reference resolution.
outputs: list of records retained under hold or as permanent
preconditions: A governed disposition authority covers every record class in scope
No legal hold applies to the record
Tombstone and lineage minimums are defined
effects: Irreversibly removes or transfers eligible records
Reduces the reconstruction horizon and records the new horizon
Preserves lineage edges and tombstones for resolvability

functions.name: Assign mandate
functions.description: Attach or withdraw a remit, purpose code and delegation source on a unit for a validity interval.
preconditions: An effective time is supplied and, where the change is material, an authorizing framework is referenced.
effects: A remit, purpose code and delegation source are attached to or withdrawn from the unit for the stated validity interval.

functions.name: Seat post in unit
functions.description: Create or attach an established post in a unit independently of any holder. Occupancy is not performed here.
preconditions: The acting party is the designated establishment function of the parent organization.
effects: An established post exists in the unit independently of any holder, and no occupancy or employment fact is asserted.

functions.name: Assert reporting line
functions.description: Record a supervisory or dotted-line reporting edge between units or posts with validity.
effects: A supervisory or dotted-line reporting edge exists between the source and target for the stated validity interval, without altering containment.

functions.name: Record staffing snapshot
functions.description: Store a dated established and filled count for a unit with basis and observation time. Treat as an extension until a primary unit-level metric standard is cited.
effects: A dated established and filled count is appended for the unit with basis and observation time, without rewriting structure.

composition.target: WM-ORG-001 Organization
composition.purpose: Every unit resolves to exactly one parent organization, which holds legal identity, registration and external identifiers. W3C ORG grounds the dependency: a unit 'only has full recognition within the context of that Organization'.

composition.target: WM-ORG-004 Position
composition.purpose: Units contain or govern established posts. This model holds the establishment count, seating and unit-level occupancy; the post as an object that 'exists independently of who fills it' is defined in WM-ORG-004.

composition.target: Employment / role assignment model
composition.purpose: Employment records fill the posts seated in a unit and are the derivation source for unit-level occupancy counts; persons and contracts never enter this model.

composition.target: Charter / constitutive powers model
composition.purpose: Unit mandates trace upward to powers held by the organization; ISO 37000 requires delegation to be formalized and delegators to remain accountable, so the upstream power must be resolvable.

composition.target: Site / Location model
composition.purpose: A unit may be associated with one or more premises, but FHIR keeps Location distinct from Organization and Eurostat's local unit is a geographic statistical construct, so premises are referenced rather than embedded.

composition.target: Stewardship model (S1)
composition.purpose: The parent organization owns the structure record and units have no independent standing; ownership, custodianship and accountability facets come from the stewardship model.

composition.target: Access grant model (S2)
composition.purpose: Disclosure classes defined here are enforced by grants issued in the access model; this model supplies the scoped projections and suppression parameters, not the grant machinery.

composition.target: Audit trail model (S4)
composition.purpose: Reorganization acts, mandate changes, waivers and disposition actions require immutable audit facets with separate event and record timestamps.

composition.target: W3C Organization Ontology (org:)
composition.purpose: Primary structural alignment for OrganizationalUnit, hasUnit/unitOf, subOrganizationOf, purpose, classification, Post, Site and ChangeEvent. Unit-to-unit reportsTo is declared an extension, since org:reportsTo binds Agents and Posts.

composition.target: Core Public Organisation Vocabulary (CPOV) v2.1.2
composition.purpose: Public-sector profile alignment for hasUnit, code-valued purpose (COFOG), classification and spatial coverage; applicable only where the parent organization is a public body.

composition.target: HL7 FHIR Organization / OrganizationAffiliation (R5)
composition.purpose: Healthcare-sector projection where departments are Organization instances chained by partOf and non-hierarchical relations use OrganizationAffiliation; a known structural conflict with the distinct-unit-class model.

composition.target: ISO/IEC 6523 organization part identification (via Peppol ICD registry)
composition.purpose: External addressing of a unit as an organization part under the parent's ICD and organization identifier, used for e-business party and delivery-location identification.

composition.target: LDAP (RFC 4519) and SCIM (RFC 7643) directory schemas
composition.purpose: Outbound-only projection targets. Both carry unit information as names without identifiers, validity or typed edges, so alignment is declared lossy and re-import is prohibited.

composition.target: Statistical units framework (Council Regulation (EEC) No 696/93)
composition.purpose: Mapping of internal units to enterprise, kind-of-activity unit and local unit for statistical reporting, recorded as a derivation with explicit boundary mismatch rather than as equivalence.

composition.target: IFRS 8 operating segment determination
composition.purpose: The internal reporting hierarchy is an input to segment identification under the management approach, and reorganization acts trigger the restate-or-disclose obligation; segment determination itself stays outside this model.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name a single parent organization as owner of every unit record; units have no independent standing and cannot own their own structure entry.

The Dimension must declare, per attribute group (identity, hierarchy, mandate, establishment, staffing), which system is master and publish the precedence order used to resolve conflicting assertions.
The Dimension must publish a governed unit-kind code list, a status vocabulary and a named hierarchy inventory before any unit record is accepted.
The Dimension must bind every structure record class to an approved disposition authority and declare its bitemporal reconstruction horizon.
The Dimension must declare its minimum cell size for staffing disclosure and the audience classes to which each projection may be released.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a Dimension-scoped namespace of the form <dimension-namespace>/org-unit/ with unit identifiers qualified by the parent organization identifier, since unit identifiers are only unique inside their parent. Do not mint global IRIs implying registry status: ROR and GLEIF do not identify internal subdivisions. Where external addressing is needed, compose an ISO/IEC 6523 triple (ICD:organizationIdentifier:organizationPartIdentifier) rather than inventing a new global scheme. Keep hierarchy, reporting-line and mandate edge types in distinct sub-namespaces so that concurrent hierarchies remain separable.
registry_links: vr.wm-org-002 (this model) under nav path NAV.SOC.ORG.UNT
vr.wm-org-001 Organization - required parent reference for every unit
vr.wm-org-004 Position - contained model for established posts
Governed unit-kind code list registered as a Dimension classifier entry
ISO/IEC 6523 ICD registry as referenced through the Peppol code list

canonicalization_rules: Serialise timestamps as RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or 'Z'; use '-00:00' only where the UTC instant is known but the local offset is not.
Order collections deterministically before digesting: units by unitIdentifier, edges by (hierarchyIdentifier, parent, child, validFrom), aliases by (type, language, validFrom).
Normalise names with Unicode NFC and preserve original casing and script; never fold case for identity purposes.
Represent open-ended validity by an explicit open marker rather than by a sentinel far-future date, so that digests do not change when conventions change.
Exclude derived elements (hierarchyPath, rollup counts, projections) from the canonical form; recompute them from asserted edges.
patch_rules: Correcting a mistaken record and recording a real-world change are different operations: corrections adjust record time only, reorganizations open and close world-time intervals.
A reorganization patch must carry decision, effective and record timestamps and must reference the deciding authority; a patch missing any of the three is rejected.
Patches are additive over the bitemporal store: no assertion is overwritten in place, and superseded intervals remain retrievable until disposition.
Identifier fields, lineage edges and issued artifacts are immutable; changing them requires a new record with an explicit supersession edge.
Backdated patches beyond the declared window require named approval and are marked so consumers can detect retroactive change.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional element, a new named hierarchy or a new code value is a minor change; removing an element, tightening cardinality or retiring a code value is a major change.
Retired unit-kind and status codes are deprecated with a successor mapping and never removed from the published code list.
Crosswalk entries are versioned against an exact target vocabulary version; a target version bump requires a new crosswalk instance and a review, not an in-place edit.

Conformance to an external standard is asserted only with a referenced test result; where a target lacks a term (for example unit-to-unit reportsTo in W3C ORG), the export declares non-conformance rather than silently coercing.
Projections never round-trip: a consumer may not submit an org chart, LDAP or SCIM export back as a source of truth.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the parent organization (unit register key, official decision reference, approved schedule reference).

Governed global identifier or IRI where one genuinely exists - an ISO/IEC 6523 ICD plus organization identifier plus organization part identifier, or an LEI where the subdivision is itself a registered legal entity.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, with the minting act recorded, used only when neither of the above exists.
A date, a name, an org-chart position or a cost centre code is never an identifier; at most they are qualifiers on an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or 'Z'. Event time (decision instant, effective instant, snapshot as-of date) and observation time (computation, ingestion, record instant) are recorded as separate fields and never conflated; '-00:00' is reserved for a known UTC instant with unknown local offset.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named <artifact-id>--<scope-key>--<as-of or effective instant in RFC 3339 basic form>--v<sequence>, where scope-key is the organization identifier plus any hierarchy, basis or target-vocabulary qualifier. The instant qualifies but never replaces the identifier, and the sequence disambiguates multiple instances sharing an instant.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every issued artifact carries a content digest over its canonical serialisation, the structureVersionId it was derived from, the rule-set or crosswalk version applied, and its loss manifest where it is a projection. Issued artifacts are immutable: corrections are new serial instances that reference the superseded one, and any artifact whose digest does not verify is treated as unusable rather than as merely stale.

policies: The parent organization is the sole authority for unit structure; no downstream system, directory or projection may originate or overwrite a structural assertion.
Reorganization is an evidenced act, not an attribute edit: every change to existence, parentage, kind or mandate requires a decision record with authority, evidence and three distinct timestamps.
Unit-level staffing is published only above the declared minimum cell size, with suppression markers distinguishing suppressed values from true zeros.
Delegated authority must be formalized with stated limits and an assurance process, and no unit may be held accountable for matters over which it holds no authority.
Lineage edges and tombstones outlive the units they connect, so that historical references remain resolvable after disbandment.
External standard mappings are alignments; conformance is claimed only with referenced test evidence, and known conflicts are published with the mapping.
Parent-organization ownership: unit records are created, changed and retired under the parent organization's authority, not by the unit itself.
Stable identity: a new master identifier or IRI is minted only when the resulting body is sufficiently distinct; otherwise update name, parent, kind or status in time.
Structure versus people: organization-chart disclosure defaults to units, kinds and reporting lines; person names, grades and headcount require an explicit grant.
Time discipline: valid-from, valid-to, decision-time and observed-at are never collapsed into a single date field, and a date is never used as an identifier.

read: Read the current unit record, its hierarchy position and its reporting lines within the requester's disclosure class.
Reconstruct any past structure state by world-time and record-time instant within the declared reconstruction horizon.
Read mandate, authority limits and establishment only with the corresponding scope; staffing figures only above the minimum cell size.
Resolve an alias, former name or external identifier to the current unit or to a tombstone with a successor pointer.
create: Create a unit only with a parent organization reference, at least one name or identifier, a kind code from the governed list and an effective instant.
Create a reorganization act with kind, affected units and roles, deciding authority, evidence reference and decision, effective and record timestamps.
Create a headcount snapshot only with a declared counting basis, population definition, as-of date and observation timestamp.
Create a mandate only with a resolvable delegating instrument and a validity period.
update: Update names, aliases and contact-style attributes directly, with record-time versioning and an actor reference.
Change existence, parentage, kind or mandate only through a reorganization act; direct edits to those fields are rejected.
Correct erroneous records through a record-time correction that preserves the prior belief rather than overwriting it.
Supersede an establishment table, authority schedule or disposition schedule by issuing a new version with an explicit predecessor link.
delete: Do not delete units to represent cessation: disband them through an act and retain the tombstone with lineage edges intact.
Withdraw records created in error using the withdrawn status with a reason, keeping the distinction from real-world cessation.
Destroy or transfer structure records only under an approved disposition authority, with no active legal hold, recording the action per record.
After disposition, publish the reduced reconstruction horizon and retain the minimum tombstone fields needed for reference resolution.

roles.name: Structure Owner (parent organization governing body)
responsibilities: Holds ultimate accountability for the structure record and approves the delegation of authority schedule.
Approves reorganization acts that create, merge, transfer or disband units.
Resolves persistent conflicts between attribute masters.

roles.name: Structure Steward
responsibilities: Maintains the unit register, the kind code list, the status vocabulary and the named hierarchy inventory.
Applies reorganization acts, opens and closes validity intervals and maintains lineage edges.
Runs validation, triages findings and tracks remediation to closure.

roles.name: Mandate and Delegation Custodian
responsibilities: Records mandates and authority limits against their delegating instruments and assurance processes.
Detects overlapping remits and segregation-of-duties breaches and manages time-bounded waivers.
Reviews delegation formalisation before a reorganization act is approved.

roles.name: Workforce Data Custodian
responsibilities: Defines counting bases and population definitions and produces dated headcount and FTE snapshots.
Reconciles authorized establishment against actual staffing and escalates variance breaches.
Applies minimum cell size suppression and logs each suppression decision.

roles.name: Records and Disclosure Officer
responsibilities: Binds record classes to an approved disposition authority and executes disposition under legal-hold checks.
Approves disclosure packages, embargoes and audience-specific projections.
Maintains the redaction manifest and the reconstruction horizon statement.

roles.name: Interoperability Custodian
responsibilities: Maintains crosswalks to W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR, LDAP, SCIM, schema.org and ISO/IEC 6523 with exact target versions.
Monitors target vocabulary version drift and schedules crosswalk reviews.
Guards against projection round-trips and publishes loss manifests with every export.

access.default_rule: Deny by default. A principal receives only the elements permitted by its disclosure class for the requested scope; unit identity, name, kind and containment position are the widest normally granted set, while mandate detail, authority limits, establishment and staffing require additional explicit scope.
exceptions: Public authorities may be obliged to publish their unit structure and purpose, so a public disclosure class may expose identity, name, kind, purpose and hierarchy without individual grant.
Auditors and assurance providers receive read access to mandate, authority limits and validation reports for a bounded engagement period without staffing detail below the minimum cell size.
Embargoed reorganization acts are withheld from all classes except the deciding body and named preparers until the release trigger, even from principals who otherwise hold structure read scope.
Employee representative bodies may receive advance access to a proposed reorganization where a jurisdictional information and consultation duty applies, ahead of general disclosure.
Emergency break-glass read of full structure requires named approval, is time-boxed, and is reported to the Structure Owner after the fact.
Classified, embargoed or security-sensitive units may be omitted from all external projections until an exception expires.
Works-council, whistleblowing or legally privileged overlays are not disclosed through this model.
LDAP userPassword and any authentication secret MUST NOT be stored or projected as unit context.
audit_requirements: Log every read of mandate, authority limit, establishment and staffing elements with principal, scope, purpose and RFC 3339 timestamp.
Log every reorganization act application with the three timestamps, deciding authority, evidence reference and validation verdict.
Log every suppression, redaction and embargo decision with the rule applied, so a consumer can distinguish suppression from absence.
Log every disposition action with the schedule reference, hold check outcome and the resulting reconstruction horizon.
Retain audit entries under the same disposition authority as the records they describe and never below the reconstruction horizon.
Create, reparent, merge, split, disband, mandate assignment and disclosure grants MUST be auditable with actor, event time and observation time.
Read of excepted units SHOULD be auditable.

read_order: AGENTS.md - identify the model, its type and the four resolvable URLs before any other action
Specification URL - read scope, boundaries and the bundle/layer/finding structure to learn what this model does and does not own
Storage type URL - learn the concrete projection (JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MongoDB or other) and the canonicalization rules; treat the projection as non-semantic
Interface URL - learn the read, create, update and delete operations, their scopes and the deny-by-default access rule
Processes URL - learn the reorganization, validation, snapshot, disclosure and disposition procedures and their preconditions
Governed code lists and hierarchy inventory - resolve unit kinds, status vocabulary and named hierarchies before writing any record
Crosswalk map - consult before emitting to any external vocabulary and honour the declared fidelity and non-conformance notes

coverage.claim: Covers the internal organizational unit as an entity: parent-scoped identity and classification, containment and concurrent hierarchies, reporting and non-hierarchical affiliation, mandate and delegated authority limits, establishment and unit-grain staffing measurement, evidenced structural change with bitemporal validity and as-of reconstruction, plus provenance, retention, disclosure and crosswalk rules. Grounded chiefly in W3C ORG, CPOV 2.1.2, FHIR R5, RFC 4519/7643/3339, ISO/IEC 6523 as deployed by Peppol, schema.org, IFRS 8, ESRS S1, ISO 37000 committee material and NARA disposition practice, with two imported W3C ORG-anchored refinements from the secondary provider. Several nodes rest on interpretation rather than normative clause text, unit-grain staffing measurement is extension-grade, and no claim of universal or metaphysical completeness is made.

checklist.notes: Parent-scoped master identifiers are treated as primary; ISO/IEC 6523 organization part identification supplies the external addressing slot; UUID/ULID is the explicit fallback. Grounded in W3C ORG, Peppol's ICD registry and schema.org iso6523Code. Falsified the assumption of a global unit registry using ROR's stated scope exclusion and GLEIF's legal-entity-only remit.

Status vocabulary separates operating, ceased and created-in-error following ROR's active/inactive/withdrawn distinction; transitions requiring a reorganization act are distinguished from corrections; tombstoning is mandated so lineage outlives units.

Containment, concurrent hierarchies, reporting lines and non-hierarchical affiliations are separated, following W3C ORG's split of hasUnit/subOrganizationOf from reportsTo and FHIR's split of partOf from OrganizationAffiliation. Unit-to-unit reporting is flagged as an extension, not conformant use.

Bitemporality is mandatory: world-time validity and record-time transaction intervals on every assertion; decision, effective and record instants on every act; RFC 3339 with explicit offset and the '-00:00' unknown-offset convention. As-of reconstruction is tied to IFRS 8's restate-or-disclose obligation.

Per-attribute-group master systems with a declared precedence order, ingestion timestamps separate from event time, evidence attachment requirements for authoritative assertions, and lineage edges carrying the act that created them.

The parent organization is the sole owner; units have no independent standing. Accountable role modelled as a post/role slot rather than a person, and ISO 37000's rule that delegators remain accountable is carried into the authority-limit finding.

Explicit rule classes: acyclicity per hierarchy, single parent per hierarchy per interval, referential integrity to WM-ORG-001 and WM-ORG-004, gap/overlap policy, FHIR's name-or-identifier minimum, and segregation constraints. Results are issued as an immutable report artifact with severity and blocking semantics.

Deny by default with bundle/layer/finding/artifact scopes; disclosure classes per projection; embargo on unannounced reorganization; break-glass is time-boxed and reported. Public-authority transparency is handled as a declared exception rather than as the default.

Disposition follows an approved authority on the NARA model where schedule use is mandatory; permanent classes (founding acts, lineage, mandate instruments) are distinguished from transitory ones; deletion is reconciled with the reconstruction horizon and with tombstone resolvability; legal holds suspend disposition.

Versioned crosswalks to W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR, LDAP, SCIM, schema.org and ISO/IEC 6523, each with direction and fidelity notes. Projection loss is declared and re-import is prohibited, because LDAP 'ou' and SCIM department/division carry only names.
Kind codes are scheme-bound and versioned, following org:classification and CPOV's code-valued purpose and classification; multi-scheme coding is supported with a governing-scheme flag.

Mandate scope, delegating instrument, quantitative authority limits, sub-delegation rules and assurance processes are modelled on ISO 37000 guidance. The full ISO 37000 text is paywalled; only the ISO/TC 309 committee overview was reviewed, so this is guidance-grade rather than requirement-grade support.

Headcount and FTE are treated as dated measurement events with declared basis, population definition, preparer and restatement handling, constrained by ESRS S1-6's headcount/FTE and breakdown requirements.

Individual occupancy is excluded by boundary; only unit-level aggregates are held; minimum cell size suppression and prohibited breakdown combinations are modelled. Specific data-protection legal bases are deferred to a privacy model.

Handled as a bounded reference: mandate spatial coverage is in scope via CPOV's spatial property, but premises, addresses and geometry are excluded because FHIR separates Location from Organization and Eurostat's local unit is a statistical geographic construct.

Communities of practice, informal influence networks, temporary task forces below the establishment threshold and de facto reporting that diverges from the recorded chart are not modelled. No authoritative source was found that normatively defines these, so they are recorded as a gap rather than invented.

Works councils, union structures and co-determination bodies interact with reorganization but are only referenced as a precondition on the act. Their own composition, election cycles and rights vary by jurisdiction and are left to a dedicated model; no primary source was retrieved during this research.

known_omissions: Full texts of ISO 37000:2021, ISO 30414:2018, ISO 15489-1:2016 and ISO/IEC 6523-1:2023 are paywalled. Only committee overview material, catalogue metadata, the Peppol ICD deployment and secondary summaries were reviewed, so ISO-derived structure is guidance-grade rather than verified against normative clause text.

Council Regulation (EEC) No 696/93 could not be retrieved directly from EUR-Lex during this research; the statistical-unit boundary rests on the Eurostat Statistics Explained glossary entry that cites it.

The ESRS S1 delegated act annex PDF was retrieved but not machine-parseable; the S1-6 headcount and breakdown requirements are stated at summary level and should be verified against clause text before any compliance claim.

Military, ecclesiastical, academic-collegiate and cooperative governance structures have unit forms (regiments, dioceses, faculties, chapters) that are not specifically accommodated beyond the generic kind code list.
Capacity and skills held by a unit, budget allocation mechanics, and process or capability ownership are deliberately excluded and would need sibling models.
No modelling of unit-level performance objectives, KPIs or scorecards; these were judged to belong to a performance-management model.
Cross-organization joint ventures and shared-service entities that sit between two parents are only partially handled through affiliations; their dual-ownership structure is unresolved.
Cost-centre, profit-centre and funds-centre hierarchies used in ERP as parallel to supervisory structure
Typed multi-hierarchy collections such as supervisory, matrix, geographic and custom trees as first-class objects
Military table of organization and equipment versus actual strength
German works-council and other co-determination overlays
Google Workspace and other directory-policy organizational units used only for inheritance
SCIM enterprise user department attributes
SAP Organization-Position-Person object model as a vendor specification
Grade, pay-scale and bargaining-unit systems
ISO 30400 vocabulary definition and the full ISO 30414 and ISO 6523 texts, which are paywalled
Informal or shadow organization
Classified intelligence structures beyond an exception flag
Temporary project organizations as a project-management class
conflicts: W3C ORG binds org:reportsTo to Agents and Posts, not to organizational units. Unit-to-unit reporting lines - which the previous O2 material asserted directly - are therefore an extension of the standard and are recorded as non-conformant use with an explicit mapping rule.

FHIR R5 has no distinct organizational-unit class: departments are Organization instances chained by partOf. This conflicts with W3C ORG's separate OrganizationalUnit class and with CPOV's reuse of it; exports to FHIR flatten the distinction and must declare the loss.

schema.org's parentOrganization (superseding branchOf) does not distinguish an internal department from an owned subsidiary, conflating containment with ownership. The crosswalk must add an edge-semantics qualifier that schema.org cannot carry.

RFC 4519 'ou' and RFC 7643 department/division are name-valued and multi-valued, with no identifier, validity period or typed edge. Round-tripping through a directory is lossy in a way that cannot be repaired, so directory content is never authoritative.

ROR and GLEIF both decline to identify internal subdivisions - ROR because departments 'often emerge, close, combine, and change', GLEIF because an LEI represents one legal entity. There is therefore no governed global identifier for most units, and ISO/IEC 6523's organization part identifier is the only standard slot, with ambiguity about who assigns it.
IFRS 8 permits aggregation of operating segments with similar economic characteristics, so a reportable segment is not a unit and a one-to-one mapping between units and segments cannot be assumed.
CPOV constrains purpose to COFOG codes suited to public administration; that scheme is inapplicable to private-sector units, so purpose coding is scheme-dependent rather than universal.

Eurostat's local unit is defined by geographic situation, whereas an internal unit is defined by mandate and reporting. Treating an office or site as an organizational unit conflates the two and produces incorrect statistical reporting.
CPOV ranges unitOf at Public Organisation and says a unit cannot exist on its own; ORG allows units of units and treats OrganizationalUnit as a subclass of Organization.
FHIR and Schema.org model departments as Organization with a single partOf or department link; ORG and LDAP use a distinct OrganizationalUnit class.
FHIR partOf is 0..1; matrix reporting in ORG is a separate reportsTo graph and must not be forced into containment.
Popolo allows only one classification and forbids org:holds; ORG allows multiple classifications and direct holds or Membership.
ORG ChangeEvent is for distinct resulting identity and URI; CPOV prev and next also cover rename and split sequences that may keep identity. Internal reorgs mostly should not mint new URIs.
Popolo and Schema.org use calendar dates for founding and dissolution; this model requires RFC 3339 date-times with offset.
LDAP uniqueMember encodes disambiguation in the name string; linked-data practice keeps a stable IRI and records former names separately.
regional_assumptions: CPOV, ESRS S1 and the statistical-unit framework are EU instruments; their applicability outside the EU is by voluntary adoption only.
NARA General Records Schedules bind US federal agencies only; they are used here as a model for governed disposition authority, not as a generally applicable rule.

Employee information and consultation duties before a reorganization takes effect vary sharply - strong in several continental European jurisdictions, weak or absent elsewhere - so consultation is modelled as an optional, jurisdiction-conditioned precondition on a reorganization act.

Public-sector units in some jurisdictions have statutory existence published in an official gazette, giving them an external authority that private units lack; the model accommodates this through the dual-classification flag but does not enumerate national regimes.
Minimum cell size thresholds for staffing disclosure are set by national data-protection practice and collective agreements, so the threshold is a Dimension parameter rather than a fixed value.
ISO/IEC 6523 ICD availability is uneven by country; the Peppol list reflects European e-invoicing deployment more densely than other regions.
Financial reporting alignment assumes IFRS; US GAAP ASC 280 uses a comparable management approach but differs in detail and was not researched.
W3C spelling organization is used in identifiers even in jurisdictions that spell organisation.
COFOG as a purpose code is a European public-sector recommendation, not a global requirement.
LDAP/X.500 distinguished-name trees remain a common enterprise projection but are not the semantic identity.
Legal personality follows the ORG FormalOrganization versus OrganizationalUnit split; jurisdictions that treat some departments as legal persons must type those as organizations, not units.
Privacy warnings assume jurisdictions that regulate publication of information about people.
adversarial_checks: Searched for a governed global identifier for internal units. ROR states it is 'not focused on capturing all subdivisions of a given organization such as a university's schools or departments' and GLEIF issues LEIs only to legal entities. The attractive assumption of a global unit IRI was rejected; unit identity is parent-scoped by default with ISO/IEC 6523 organization part identification as the only standard external slot.

Tested whether unit-to-unit reporting lines have standards support. W3C ORG defines org:reportsTo between Agents or Posts, not units, so the previous version's unit-level reportingLine object is an extension. Retained because matrix management is real, but demoted to a declared non-conformant extension rather than presented as canonical.

Tested whether sites, offices and branches belong in this model. FHIR states Location records where a service occurs while Organization records who performed it, and Eurostat's local unit is defined by geographic situation. Rejected folding premises into unit structure; branches that are separately registered are handled by dual classification instead.

Tested whether established positions belong here or in WM-ORG-004. W3C ORG's Post 'exists independently of who fills it', and the registry assigns Position its own model, so only the unit-side establishment count, seating and aggregate occupancy were retained. The previous version's full establishedPosition object was rejected as a boundary violation.

Tested whether a single containment tree is sufficient. IFRS 8's management approach makes the internal reporting hierarchy decisive for segment identification, which may differ from the legal or cost roll-up. Single-parent-only structure was rejected in favour of named concurrent hierarchies with per-hierarchy single-parent constraints.

Tested whether reorganization can be modelled as attribute edits on unit records. W3C ORG's ChangeEvent with originalOrganization and resultingOrganization requires many-to-many lineage that attribute edits cannot express, and ROR retains relationships on inactive records as tombstones. Attribute-edit modelling was rejected.

Tested whether directory and HR systems could serve as the source of truth. RFC 4519 and RFC 7643 carry unit information as bare names without identifiers, validity or typed edges, so any round-trip silently destroys governed structure. Re-import was prohibited outright rather than merely discouraged.

Tested whether headcount is a unit attribute. ESRS S1-6 requires declared basis, breakdowns and methodology disclosure, and figures differ by point-in-time versus average convention. Attribute modelling was rejected in favour of dated measurement events with an explicit basis and separate observation timestamp.
Could a legally registered subsidiary be stored as an OrganizationalUnit and thereby lose world-facing identity? Reject: use WM-ORG-001.
Can a matrix unit with two bosses be stored with two partOf parents in a FHIR projection? Reject: one containment parent, extra reportsTo edges.
Does renaming the Finance unit require a new IRI? No, unless a ChangeEvent declares a distinct resulting body.
Does publishing an org chart that names heads process personal data? Yes; use a structure-only projection unless a grant covers names.
Is a standing committee a unit, a post, or an OrganizationalCollaboration? If it exists only inside one parent as a subdivision, it may be a unit; if it spans organizations, it is not.
Can a vacant established post keep the unit chart intact? Yes; Post exists without a holder.
If a disbanded battalion name is reused, is the new unit the same record? No; assign a new master identifier or a disambiguator.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently classify WM-ORG-002 as an entity, and the base draws the boundary on every side with source-referenced neighbour distinctions: legal personality to WM-ORG-001 (W3C ORG FormalOrganization vs OrganizationalUnit; GLEIF issues LEIs only to legal entities), the post as an object to WM-ORG-004 (org:Post exists independently of its holder), premises to a site model (FHIR Location vs Organization), statistical observation units to a statistics model (Reg. 696/93), and derived segments to financial reporting (IFRS 8 management approach with permitted aggregation). Directory content (RFC 4519 ou, RFC 7643 department) is fixed as a lossy projection and never a system of record. The one live boundary disagreement is the unit-to-site association, which the secondary provider places in scope; the base exclusion is retained for this pass and the association is deferred rather than forced into a layer that does not fit it.

decisions.rationale: Not chosen for size. The base states in_scope, out_of_scope and seven source-referenced neighbour distinctions that close the boundary on every side, and its adversarial checks show the boundary was tested rather than asserted. The secondary provider leaves the site boundary open and treats multi-hierarchy structure as an omission.

Both providers converge on entity independently, and the node behaves as a persistent identified thing with lifecycle, relationships and versioned state rather than as an event, a policy or a service.

Fills a gap the base itself declares unresolved, is anchored in the base's own tier-1 source, and supplies the test that keeps cross-organization bodies out of the unit set instead of silently absorbing them.
Prevents the base from over-claiming ORG semantics by treating every rename or reparent as a ChangeEvent, and adds CPOV hasFormalFramework as the link from the act to its authorizing instrument.

Genuinely evidence-backed in W3C ORG via org:Site, hasSite, hasPrimarySite and hasRegisteredSite, and therefore not rejected on evidence. But the base excludes premises by explicit adversarial decision and no existing base layer hosts a placement finding, so importing it would require inventing structure. Held open as a boundary question.

The base already covers master-system assignment, ISO/IEC 6523 organization-part addressing, identifier stability across rename and reparent, and the UUID/ULID fallback. Only the point that an LDAP distinguished name is a naming address rather than a persistent identifier is additive, and it belongs as a crosswalk note on projection fidelity, not a new finding.

The base's naming finding already carries official name, aliases, former names and the rule that names are never identity. The SKOS prefLabel/altLabel/notation binding and CPOV's at-most-one-preferred-label-per-language cardinality are refinements to that finding, to be folded into the crosswalk rather than added as separate structure.

The base's accountable-role finding already models the head as a post or Membership slot with acting, interim and vacant states and keeps person occupancy out of scope. org:headOf as a specialization of memberOf is a mapping detail for the crosswalk.

The base's mandate-scope finding covers remit statement, delegating instrument, spatial and functional limits, and the CPOV COFOG recommendation with its public-sector restriction already recorded as a conflict.

decisions.disposition: rejected as a finding, escalated to a hold
decisions.rationale: Duplicates the base's authorized-post-complement, but carries a caveat the base lacks: neither W3C ORG nor the ISO material consulted defines establishment counts, grades or pay bands, so those are local controls rather than standard properties. That evidentiary limit is recorded as a publication hold instead of new structure.

The base's unit-lineage finding covers predecessor and successor edges, identifier continuity, tombstone dereferencing and partial transfer in a split. CPOV prev/next and the dual-running overlap window are deferred as crosswalk and validation detail.

establish-unit, reparent-unit, merge-or-split-units and disband-unit are decompositions of the base's apply-reorganization-act, which already opens and closes validity intervals, creates lineage edges and registers downstream obligations. Importing them would fork the write path.

The base already separates derive-org-chart, which deliberately omits mandate and staffing, from the structure-disclosure package and its scoping rules; a second disclosure entry point would blur that separation.

Both providers agree org:reportsTo is defined between Agents and Posts. The base's stricter treatment of unit-level edges as a declared non-conformant extension with a mapping rule governs, and the imported assert-reporting-line function must write that declaration.

The base marks measurement covered on ESRS S1-6, which is an undertaking-level disclosure standard, while the secondary provider marks it a gap because no primary source defines a unit-grain metric. The honest position is that unit-level headcount and FTE are operationally necessary but standards-thin.

The base models managerial, legal, cost and functional hierarchies as separately governed edge sets with per-hierarchy single-parent constraints and ties the choice to IFRS 8's management approach; the secondary provider lists typed multi-hierarchy collections as an omission, so the base is strictly stronger here.

publicationHolds: Source and live-version verification is outstanding for all sixteen base sources and for the two imported W3C ORG and CPOV anchors. Resolve the dated W3C ORG REC URI against the latest-version URI, confirm CPOV 2.1.2, schema.org v30.0 and the Peppol ICD list are still current, and pin FHIR deliberately, since the base cites R5 and the secondary provider cites R4.

ISO-derived structure is guidance-grade, not requirement-grade. ISO 37000:2021, ISO 30414:2018, ISO 15489-1:2016 and ISO/IEC 6523-1:2023 are paywalled and were reviewed only through committee decks, catalogue metadata and deployment profiles, so the delegated-authority, assurance and segregation findings must not be published as normatively sourced until clause text is verified.

ESRS S1-6 clause text was not machine-parsed; headcount, FTE, breakdown and the fifty-employee country threshold are stated at summary level and must be checked against Annex I of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 before any compliance-adjacent claim.

Unit-grain staffing measurement has no primary standard. Established-versus-filled counts, budgeted FTE and establishment complement are local controls; publish the measurement layer and record-staffing-snapshot as extension-grade with that limitation visible.

Multi-profile validation is incomplete. The model was tested chiefly against public-sector (CPOV/COFOG), healthcare (FHIR), EU reporting (IFRS 8, ESRS S1), directory (LDAP/SCIM) and e-invoicing (ISO/IEC 6523) profiles. Private-sector matrix organizations, military, academic-collegiate, ecclesiastical and cooperative unit forms are not validated and must not be presented as covered.

Council Regulation (EEC) No 696/93 was not retrieved from EUR-Lex; the statistical-unit boundary currently rests on a Eurostat glossary entry that cites it, and must be confirmed against the regulation text.

Regional scope must be stated on the face of any draft: CPOV, ESRS and the statistical-unit framework are EU instruments, NARA General Records Schedules bind US federal agencies only, financial alignment assumes IFRS rather than ASC 280, and employee consultation duties before a reorganization are jurisdiction-conditioned.
deferredResearch: Unit-to-site association: decide whether org:hasSite, hasPrimarySite and hasRegisteredSite belong here as a bounded reference or entirely in the site model. The base excludes premises after an explicit adversarial test; the secondary provider places the link in scope on W3C ORG evidence. Resolve before the next boundary pass, and add a placement layer only if the reference is accepted.

CPOV range and lineage detail: CPOV ranges unitOf at Public Organisation and states a unit cannot exist on its own, which is narrower than W3C ORG's units-of-units, and CPOV prev/next cover rename and split sequences that may retain identity. Fold both into the crosswalk with explicit range, cardinality and fidelity notes.

Popolo Organization and Post as an additional crosswalk target, including its single-classification restriction, its rejection of org:holds in favour of Membership, and its distinct former-name property, which few vocabularies provide.

Cost-centre, profit-centre and funds-centre ERP hierarchies: confirm whether these are admitted as named concurrent hierarchies inside this model or remain finance masters referenced from it, since both providers flag them and neither resolves the boundary.

Works councils, union structures and co-determination bodies: both providers record these as an unmodelled gap that nonetheless gates reorganization effectiveness. Determine whether they become a sibling model or remain a jurisdiction-conditioned precondition on the act.

Establishment-count standardization: search for a primary, unit-grain source defining authorized post complement, grade and budgeted FTE. Absent one, keep the establishment findings marked as local control rather than standard property.

LDAP distinguished-name instability under reparenting, and the name-reuse-after-disbandment collision case with x500UniqueIdentifier-style disambiguators, as validation rules on the identity and projection-fidelity findings.

Informal and shadow structure, temporary project organizations and de facto reporting: both providers record these as gaps with no authoritative source. Confirm the gap stands rather than inventing structure to close it.
